reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text three times against a saved copy of Frere's Old Deccan Days tale XV.

Owner rule 2026-10-17 (never change plot or ending): Frere's ending kept, the angry crows steal the food and fly away; the earlier added lesson removed; the thorns-in-the-eyes plea restored. All five excuses in Frere's order.
The plea is ನಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಒಳಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸಿಕೋ (let us in), matching the open doorway in every panel and Frere's wording. Names, the food, the morning discovery and the crows sharing the complaint are disclosed.
Age 8+: storm, a long wait and theft; nobody injured; contentNote says so plainly.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536; seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; under 650 KB.
Exactly two crows and three chicks in every panel; the crows' nest made sparse and the final basket emptied (a few grains, no roti) in one edit pass, two panels composited.
No people, no modern objects, no pecking or injury.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher, folklorist or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol in the new stylized 3D look for this collection, and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with seams measured in pixels.
Frere recorded the tale in the Deccan from one teller; it is presented as a South Indian tale, not claimed as specifically Kannada.
